tagline: Pink siam tulip fields in the rains, the stone pillars of Mo Hin Khao, and Ban Khwao silk
introHtml: Chaiyaphum sits where Isan meets the central and northern regions, so the land is a mix of mountains and plains. For most people the province means one thing: the fields of pink-purple siam tulips that bloom across Pa Hin Ngam early in the rainy season — the image the province is known for. There's also Mo Hin Khao, a cluster of sandstone pillars standing in an open field, the Tat Ton waterfall near town where locals come to swim, and Ban Khwao, a village that has woven silk for generations. The town itself is small and easy to get around, with the Phaya Lae monument as its heart. Come to Chaiyaphum for nature and mountains, and pick up some silk to take home.
bestTime: June–August is when the siam tulips bloom at Pa Hin Ngam and Sai Thong, while November–January brings cool, comfortable weather that's good for heading up the mountains for waterfalls and views.

highlights.name: Siam tulip fields, Pa Hin Ngam
highlights.blurb: Fields of pink-purple siam tulips that bloom in early rainy season — the image the province is known for. People come every year to walk through and take photos.

highlights.name: Mo Hin Khao
highlights.blurb: A cluster of large sandstone pillars standing in an open field in Phu Laenkha National Park. Locals call it Thailand's Stonehenge — you can walk all the way around for photos.

highlights.name: Tat Ton Waterfall
highlights.blurb: A waterfall near town where the water spreads across a wide rock shelf. There's plenty of water in the rains, and people from town like to come swim and picnic on weekends.

highlights.name: Ban Khwao silk
highlights.blurb: The province's old silk-weaving center, with mudmee patterns and local silk to buy as gifts right at the village.

highlights.name: Phaya Lae Monument
highlights.blurb: The monument to the founder of Chaiyaphum and the heart of the town, with an annual offering ceremony and a steady stream of people coming to pay respects.

highlights.name: Pha Daeng, Sai Thong National Park
highlights.blurb: A cliff viewpoint in Sai Thong National Park looking out over ridges and wide plains as far as you can see. Siam tulips bloom here in the rains too.

foodScene.name: Isan food
foodScene.note: Som tam, larb, koi, grilled chicken — bold, true Isan flavors you'll find in every district. It's the everyday meal for people in Chaiyaphum.

foodScene.name: Korat mee and noodles
foodScene.note: Being next to Korat, mee phat and noodle soups are easy to find around town, at friendly local prices.

foodScene.name: Grilled fish and riverside food
foodScene.note: Around the dams and reservoirs there are spots for grilled fish, steamed fish, and fish tom yum — good for sitting by the water in the breeze.

foodScene.name: Khao mao and local sweets
foodScene.note: Khao mao tossed with coconut and homestyle sweets turn up at the morning markets — simple snacks and gifts to take home.

foodScene.name: Moo kratha
foodScene.note: Moo kratha (DIY grill-and-hotpot) joints are all over town and a popular dinner for locals, especially on weekends when groups go together.

foodScene.name: Cafes and coffee in town
foodScene.note: A number of new cafes have opened in town — a good place to sit with a coffee before heading out to the waterfalls or up the mountains.

foodScene.name: Evening market street food
foodScene.note: The evening market in town has grilled and fried snacks and desserts to graze on after dark, and it won't cost much.

foodScene.name: Forest finds and local vegetables
foodScene.note: In the rains, the districts near the mountains bring mushrooms, bamboo shoots, and local vegetables to market — good for curries and eating with nam phrik.

attractions.name: Pa Hin Ngam National Park
attractions.blurb: Home to the siam tulip fields, the oddly shaped Lan Hin Ngam rock formations, and the Sut Phaen Din viewpoint looking out over wide ridges.

attractions.name: Mo Hin Khao
attractions.blurb: A cluster of large sandstone pillars standing in an open field in Phu Laenkha park. You can walk around the whole thing for photos — locals call it Thailand's Stonehenge.

attractions.name: Tat Ton Waterfall
attractions.blurb: A wide rock-shelf waterfall near town with plenty of water in the rains — a popular swimming and picnic spot for people in the province.

attractions.name: Sai Thong National Park
attractions.blurb: A mountain park with Pha Daeng, Pha Iang, and siam tulip fields in the rains. The viewpoints look out over ridges and wide plains.

attractions.name: Phaya Lae Monument
attractions.blurb: The monument to the founder of Chaiyaphum and the heart of the town, with an annual offering ceremony and people always stopping to pay respects.

attractions.name: Ban Khwao silk-weaving village
attractions.blurb: The province's old silk-weaving village. Watch the weaving and buy mudmee silk in local patterns right at the source.

attractions.name: Prang Ku
attractions.blurb: A Khmer ruin near town, once a hospital chapel in the reign of Jayavarman VII. You can walk among the remains of laterite stonework.

attractions.name: Chulabhorn Dam
attractions.blurb: A mountain dam in the Khon San area, cool and comfortable, with reservoir viewpoints and lodging set among the ridges.
